base_setup_commands: apt-get install -y git curl cmake build-essential libomp-dev
setup_runtime_commands: Install Miniforge conda if not present
Install base dependencies: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, pytest, cmake, ninja, setuptools, wheel, pip
Install additional Python packages: dataclasses, dask, pyarrow, matplotlib, joblib, cloudpickle, psutil
Initialize git submodules for external libraries
Build C++ library with CMake: cmake -B build -S . -DUSE_OPENMP=ON
Install Python package with precompiled library: ./build-python.sh install --precompile --no-isolation
Reinstall from local sdist to ensure correct version
activation_validation_command: bash -c 'source /opt/conda/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate lightgbm-env && python -c "import lightgbm; print(\"OK\")"'

prepare_commands: conda create -q -y -n lightgbm-env python=3.11 numpy scipy scikit-learn pandas pytest cmake ninja setuptools wheel pip
pip install dataclasses dask pyarrow matplotlib joblib cloudpickle psutil
runtime_profile.test_only_install_strategy: The test dependencies (pytest, cloudpickle, psutil) are already installed in the base environment
runtime_profile.notes: LightGBM uses conda/mamba for environment management. The Python package wraps a CMake-built C++ library. Git submodules must be initialized for external libraries (fast_double_parser, eigen, fmt, compute).

notes: Base image should be Ubuntu 22.04 or similar. Git and curl are included in baseline system packages. The environment uses conda for Python environment management with pip for additional packages. LightGBM requires CMake to build the C++ library and git submodules for external dependencies. The fix.patch removes --user flags from pip install commands in CI scripts to prevent cross-job contamination.
